newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish central bank considers rate rise - paper.
newsitem.headline: Polish central bank considers rate rise - paper.

text.p: National Bank of Poland (NBP) President Hanna Gronkiewicz-Waltz signalled the central bank might raise its official interest rates if fast credit expansion continues, Nowa Europa newspaper said on Tuesday.
The paper quoted Gronkiewicz-Waltz as saying that this year's 15-16 percent real growth in credit threatened to lead to higher inflation in the second half of 1997 and called for the NBP's reaction.
"The central bank cannot just look on," Gronkiewicz-Waltz said, adding that a possible interest rate increase would be limited.
"If NBP interest rates rise, it won't be a significant move. The increase will be a signal for banks that they should not count on a further reduction in interest rates in the near future," she said.
But Nowa Europa quoted Gronkiewicz-Waltz as saying that the approval of a higher 1997 budget deficit of 2.8 percent of gross domestic product could mean that a single rate rise might not be enough.
In October the central bank said it wanted to keep its Lombard and discount rates, now at 25 percent and 22 percent respectively.
Since then it has repeatedly hinted that higher rates might be needed to cap fast credit growth.
But so far it has stopped short of making it clear whether it was referring to real or market rates or if it also considered an increase in nominal official rates.
